title: Provisioning tool: hcloud CLI default, raw Hetzner Cloud API alternative, Terraform rejected
context: An applying project needs a documented answer to how the provisioner shells out to Hetzner Cloud. Options considered: hcloud CLI (small, self-documenting, JSON output on --output json, per https://github.com/hetznercloud/cli); the raw Hetzner Cloud REST API (no CLI dependency, useful when the target host cannot install a binary, per https://docs.hetzner.cloud/); Terraform (declarative, adds a second toolchain and a state file). maintainer ruling 2026-09-07 09:50Z of the round-7 summary: hcloud not Terraform. Terraform adds a second toolchain and a state file that nobody in the estate needs.
decision: The shipped v1.0.0 default is the hcloud CLI as the provisioning tool. Alternative elicited: raw-api (the provisioner fetches the Hetzner Cloud REST API directly). Terraform is a rejected alternative recorded in the blueprint README section 9 rejected-alternatives. elicited: true. recommendedDefault: hcloud. Standards trace clause: Hetzner Cloud CLI documented resource verbs per hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07.md.
consequences: The applying project installs the hcloud binary on the operator laptop and every CI runner that provisions. The raw-api fork sits behind the same provisioner facade so no consumer code diverges. The provisioner-facade sole-reader guarantee holds on both paths.

alternativesConsidered.summary: Terraform declaring the Hetzner resources with the hetznercloud provider.
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Adds a second toolchain and a state file. The state file becomes a new source of truth to reconcile with git and with the live account. maintainer ruling 2026-09-07 09:50Z.
